chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Everything is submissive to the believer.' Then he (peace be upon him) added: 'If his heart is sincere to Allah, Allah will cause everything to fear him, even the creeping things of the earth, its beasts, and the birds of the sky.'

key_terms.هَوَامَّ الْأَرْضِ: creeping things / vermin of the earth

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of sincerity on a believer's relationship with creation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia* highlights the concept of *Nubuwwat al-Asghar* (minor prophethood) or spiritual dominion, where the believer’s *Ikhlas* (sincerity) transforms their relationship with the natural world. It illustrates that true humility before Allah results in external creatures fearing the believer, serving as a tangible sign of their elevated spiritual station and purity of heart.

en.badr-shahin: (The same previous series of relaters)… from Mohammed bin Ahmed from … Safwan al-Jammal

that he heard Abu Abdullah (a) saying: Everything is submissive to the believer. He (a) then added: Allah will cause everything, including vermin, beasts, and birds, to fear the believer if he is sincere to Allah.
